title: External review: runtime outcomes and executable admission
outcome: ACP preserves ordered session and terminal facts, long turns stay valid, Muse results remain truthful, and task/wave Start leads to valid dispatch.

tasks.title: Preserve ACP session binding and observed terminal responses
tasks.body:
## Problem and outcome
External findings: B4,B5.
handleResponse deletes pending session/new before NewSession commits c.session. awaitCall can choose EOF/deadline despite a matched response already queued. Keep a validated provisional session binding through handoff, or commit it before subsequent frames; reconcile a settled matched result/error before classifying closure as unknown. Preserve malformed-response and session-mismatch rejection. Rebase on the safety wave teardown changes; do not undo its lock discipline.

## Verified seams and ownership
- `internal/acp/client.go`
- `internal/acp/client_test.go`
Trace the named producer, consumer and every caller before editing. Own only this bounded correction and its focused checks; shared files are not blanket rewrite authority.

## Acceptance
| ID | Required observation |
| --- | --- |
| A1 | session/new response immediately followed by session/update in the same write binds to the correct session without poisoning; malformed/mismatched IDs still fail. Cover the analogous restore handoff. |
| A2 | When a valid matched terminal result or RPC error and EOF/deadline are simultaneously observable, the matched result/error wins deterministically. |
| A3 | EOF after delivery without a matched response remains delivery_unknown; no success is invented from transport exit alone. |

## Verification
| Covers | Check | Result | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1,A2,A3 | command: go test ./internal/acp -run 'TestExternalReviewSettlement' -count=1 | pending | Add controlled ordering tests, including error responses, deadline race and no-response EOF. |

## Decisions and boundaries
Keep existing public actions, canonical transitions, project/record identity, ownership, proof and budget checks. Reuse the existing implementation and storage; no parallel scheduler/store/framework. Any deliberate compatibility change beyond the listed defect returns to the operator. The task body and shared context are the handoff; external review text supplies rationale, not permission to expand scope.

tasks.title: Support informational ACP extensions and long permission-heavy turns
tasks.body:
## Problem and outcome
External findings: B7,B8.
handleRequest ignores four named Devin extensions but poisons unknown informational extensions; permissionInvocations is a lifetime counter capped at 64. Ignore valid underscore-prefixed notifications without executing them after existing envelope/frame validation. Retain method-not-found for unsupported requests. Bound live permission handlers and pending responses, releasing handler capacity only when the actual handler exits, including after cancellation.

## Verified seams and ownership
- `internal/acp/client.go`
- `internal/acp/client_test.go`
Trace the named producer, consumer and every caller before editing. Own only this bounded correction and its focused checks; shared files are not blanket rewrite authority.

## Acceptance
| ID | Required observation |
| --- | --- |
| A1 | Existing and previously unknown valid underscore-prefixed notifications do not poison startup or a prompt; unsupported requests still receive method-not-found and malformed/oversized frames retain rejection. |
| A2 | More than 64 sequential permission requests in one prompt succeed with bounded simultaneous work. |
| A3 | Non-returning handlers retain their capacity until they exit, even after caller cancellation; concurrent requests cannot grow handler count without bound or reuse capacity early. |

## Verification
| Covers | Check | Result | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1,A2,A3 | command: go test ./internal/acp -run 'TestExternalReviewPermissions' -count=1 | pending | Add sequential and stuck-handler checks using existing fake transport/handler fixtures. |

tasks.title: Preserve Muse native terminal outcomes in bounded execution
tasks.body:
## Problem and outcome
External findings: B6.
The production bounded monitor bypasses classifyMuseCLIOutput. Reuse that decoder and carry completed/failed/cancelled/missing-terminal evidence through final daemon exit classification, including review runs. Overflow and explicit cancellation take precedence. Rebase on wrapper containment changes; do not alter provider profiles or add a second decoder.

## Verified seams and ownership
- `cmd/tusker/runner_raw_log_limit.go`
- `cmd/tusker/runner_raw_log_limit_test.go`
- `cmd/tusker/runner_muse.go`
- `cmd/tusker/runner_muse_test.go`
Trace the named producer, consumer and every caller before editing. Own only this bounded correction and its focused checks; shared files are not blanket rewrite authority.

## Acceptance
| ID | Required observation |
| --- | --- |
| A1 | Process exit zero plus native failed/cancelled/missing terminal is never classified succeeded; completed terminal with valid exit is correctly classified. |
| A2 | Overflow and explicit cancellation keep their authoritative outcomes; nonzero exit cannot be converted to success by a completed native record. |
| A3 | Execute and review lanes observe the same typed terminal classification through the production bounded path and final classifier. |

## Verification
| Covers | Check | Result | Notes |

tasks.title: Allow valid lifecycle members when arming a wave
tasks.body:

directWaveArmContractBlockers accepts current status and skips readiness, but dispatch validation still rejects next_owner blocked_dependency/none/reviewer. tasks.title: Make an authorized standalone backlog Start reach dispatch
tasks.body:

External findings: C3.
directRunCmd/taskStart queue a directive, but daemon candidate filtering excludes standalone backlog before consulting it. Promote only valid directive-authorized backlog work before the active-state filter, persisting canonical state under existing CAS discipline before claiming. Reuse directive matching and control projection paths; preserve artifact-retention edits in daemon.go.
